answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity to staked capital that decays unless it keeps attesting honestly. Each agent posts a bond, then acts like a beacon: it periodically signs fresh observations, and peers keep a crystal-clear ledger of which signatures matched reality. New agents grow reputation slowly, like a lotus rising one ring at a time, so flooding the network with fake wallets costs more than it earns and votes are weighted by proven track record, not raw account count.
